summary: Early-stage inbound from a B2B SaaS vendor building an in-app concierge for SMB customers. Primary need: low-latency streaming chat for contextual, account-aware replies plus function/tool calling to pull account metadata. Prefers self-serve hosted API but needs quick answers on security/retention before a pilot.
notes: Lead came via signup funnel + product tour — used hosted API sandbox.
They are latency-sensitive: target p95 end-to-end < 150ms on short chats (<= 60 tokens) — mobile-heavy users.
Streaming is must-have — want token-by-token UI with immediate partials; asked about SDK examples for WebSockets/Server-Sent Events.
Model preference: open models (Llama2-like) if performance/cost acceptable; open to Redwood-verified models. Cost sensitive — looking for clear per-token pricing and burst options.
Context and state: will pass last 6 messages + account metadata; needs KV caching for repeated prompts to reduce cost.
Security ask: SOC2 proof, option to disable request logging for PII routes, SSO for internal users. Also wants audit log export and 30-day retention default with configurable longer options.
Quote from PM: "We need the assistant to feel instant on mobile — if streaming feels sluggish we won't ship it."
Technical ask: sample streaming key + example showing function calling to fetch account balance and recent activity. SE requested to supply a minimal repro app.
AE notes: good inbound intent, primary decision maker is Head of Product (R. Kim), budget small for pilot but may expand if latency and cost targets met.
Suggested offering: hosted API with burstable capacity, clear docs for streaming, and an initial 30-day pilot pricing cap.
Potential upsell later: Dedicated for predictable throughput if pilot scales and they need stronger isolation.
requirements: P95 latency < 150ms for short sessions (mobile network assumptions)
Ability to opt-out of request logging for routes handling PII
Audit log export and retention controls (default 30 days)
Function/tool calling with low overhead (fast cold-start for function calls)
Model fallback policy: auto-route to smaller quantized model when cost threshold reached
